Welcome to the Merrikhi Lab

We study how the brain and cognitive processes work together to support speech perception and production.

Our research focuses particularly on how working memory and attention interact with the neural systems involved in speech. We examine these processes in healthy individuals and clinical populations with communication disorders across the lifespan.

By combining behavioral research with neurophysiological methods, brain stimulation, computational approaches, and artificial intelligence, we seek to understand how speech is planned, monitored, controlled, and learned—and how this knowledge can inform more effective and personalized approaches to communication disorders.

Our goal

To connect fundamental discoveries about cognition, brain function, and speech with new ways to understand individual differences and improve communication outcomes.

SpeechCognitionEEGBrain stimulationComputational methodsArtificial intelligence

Our Research

Our work sits at the intersection of speech science, cognitive neuroscience, biomedical engineering, and computational methods.

Speech & Cognition

We investigate how cognitive processes—particularly working memory and attention—interact with speech perception and production.

Brain & Speech

We study the neural mechanisms that allow the brain to plan, produce, monitor, and adapt speech, and how these processes vary across the lifespan.

Communication Disorders & AI

We use neuroscience, brain stimulation, computational methods, and artificial intelligence to better understand communication disorders and help inform personalized interventions.
